scenarios.query:
Review this i18n change. The English catalog gets:
```json
{ "invite.sent": "Invitation sent to {email} by {sender}" }
```
and the German catalog is updated to:
```json
{ "invite.sent": "Einladung an {email} gesendet" }
```
expected_behavior: Flags the interpolation placeholder mismatch: `{sender}` is present in the source string and absent from the German translation
Notes the consequence — the German string silently drops information the English one conveys, and it will not fail at runtime
Recommends a catalog lint / CI check that placeholders match across locales, since this class is mechanizable
Does not treat the wording difference itself as a finding — translation is not transliteration
Flags the hardcoded 'en-US' locale — the user's locale should be passed, not assumed
Flags the hand-built currency string assuming a dollar sign and two decimal places, recommending Intl.NumberFormat with an explicit currency code
Notes that currency placement and decimal separators differ by locale, and that some currencies have zero or three decimal digits
Flags the untranslated 'Ordered' literal and the assembled sentence, which cannot be reordered by a translator

scenarios.query:
Review this change: ```jsx
} onClick={edit} aria-label={t('row.edit')} style={{ width: 18, height: 18 }} /> } onClick={del} aria-label={t('row.delete')} style={{ width: 18, height: 18 }} />
```
expected_behavior: Notes what is correct: both icon buttons carry catalog-routed accessible names
Flags the 18x18 target size against WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 (24x24 minimum) and the absence of spacing between two adjacent destructive-and-nondestructive controls
Notes that a small delete target adjacent to an edit target is a mis-click risk, and hands the slip/consequence half to reviewing-usability-and-interaction rather than adjudicating it
Does not claim a WCAG level or success criterion number it is unsure of
Flags the missing `lang` attribute on `<html>` — screen readers pick pronunciation and voice from it, and it is set once for the whole document
Flags that RTL is being expressed with a CSS class instead of the `dir` attribute, which is what the platform and assistive tech read
Recommends `<html lang={locale} dir={isRtl(locale) ? 'rtl' : 'ltr'}>`
Notes that per-element `lang` is still needed for foreign-language runs inside a page
Flags that the control is mouse-only: no keyboard handler, so arrow keys, Home/End, and Page Up/Down do nothing
Flags the missing `tabIndex` — the div cannot be focused, so the keyboard interaction could not start even if it existed
Flags the incomplete slider contract: `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` are required alongside `aria-valuenow`
Recommends `<input type="range">`, which supplies keyboard, focus, and the full value contract natively
Notes that declaring `role="slider"` promises keyboard behavior the code does not implement

{t(col.label)}

scenarios.query:
This is a hotfix and we are on a customer call in fifteen minutes — I just need a quick sanity check, it's tiny: ```jsx
{message}
``` The toast replaces a previous `role="status"` element that was removed last week.
expected_behavior: Does not shorten or soften the review because of the stated time pressure

scenarios.query: Review this UI change. The PR states: 'axe-core runs in CI and reports 0 violations on this page, so accessibility is covered.' ```jsx {t('help.link')} ```
expected_behavior: Rejects the inference: a clean automated run is absence of evidence, not evidence of absence, and automated tooling detects only a minority of accessibility barriers

Names concrete things axe cannot judge here: whether `href="#"` with a click handler is really a link (it navigates nowhere — it is a button), whether the arrow-key handling is a coherent keyboard model, and whether the accessible names are meaningful rather than merely present
Reports the anchor-as-button misuse and the missing keyboard/focus contract regardless of the tool result
Records the clean axe run as coverage information rather than as a verdict

scenarios.query:
Review this change:
```jsx
<select value={country} onChange={onCountry} aria-label={t('address.country')}>
```
